blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The first passenger train in India ran between Mumbai (Bori Bunder) and Thane on April 16, 1853, covering 34 km.
Indian Railways was nationalized in 1951 and currently operates through 18 distinct administrative zones.
Bholu, an elephant dressed as a railway guard, serves as the official mascot of Indian Railways.
The Vivek Express covers the longest train route in India, running from Dibrugarh in Assam to Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu.
Kolkata hosts the headquarters for three railway zones: Eastern Railway, South Eastern Railway, and Metro Railway.
Southern Railway was established on April 14, 1951, as the first railway zone created in independent India.
The Chenab Rail Bridge in Jammu & Kashmir stands as the world's highest railway arch bridge.
